lens: The words: amount, AI mentions, the work's own vocabulary, scope qualifiers, process leakage, and AGENTS.md set beside the README
in_one_paragraph: The README's first paragraph is already AGENTS.md's "What we are doing" almost word for word; what makes the page "not that" is everything put around and inside it. AGENTS says it in 222 words, 11 sentences averaging 20 words, no number, no reference, no qualifier, and ends "This is what we want. Say it plainly." The README's first screen says it in 1,328 words (its own stated 11 to 14 minutes), sentences averaging 35 words and reaching 88, 39 links, 37 numbers, 6 chapter-section references, about 27 scope qualifiers, and opens with "This version is still being revised." It drops the one sentence of AGENTS a stranger would recognise ("The wisdom exists, but we cannot coordinate") and inserts a 58-word theorem with three hypotheses as its third sentence. The growth is recent and measurable: the first screen was 166 words and "1–2 minutes" on 6 November and is 8 times that five days later; the "one page" went from 1,154 words (31 October) to 3,794 and now states 29 to 37 minutes; the "hour layer" states 86 to 112. The same 200-word opening paragraph is pasted at the top of README, one page, overview, USES, MAP and the site description, so a reader following the suggested path reads it four or five times. "How far it has been seen" is said in at least eight places for the lock theorem alone instead of once. The word "read" appears 22 times on the first screen in about seven senses. AI as authorship is one sentence on the home page (that instruction was followed there), but "AI" appears 8 times on that screen in five different roles, 15 on the one page, 36 on the overview (16 of them inline "[AI reading]" labels) and 175 in LINEAGE. One caution against a naive fix: AGENTS.md is plain for collaborators, not for strangers; it uses nine of the work's own terms in 222 words, so copying it harder will not make the page readable. Two registers are needed, and the truthfulness rule can be kept by carrying status in the verb ("can", "is proved", "was tested", "we argue", "we want") plus one "how far" page, not in subordinate clauses.

findings.what: What was asked before, verbatim, and what was not found. AI mentions: 19 Oct, "don't mention ai, me, or you. knowledge doesn't care about names, it is what it is"; 8 Nov, "we only need to briefly mention ai - it simply isn't the point. the point is the work." Length: 31 Oct, "you can easily read 100k tokens, but we as human can not". Readers' confidence: 2 Nov, "an elegant finish that is representable, and can confidently make our readers see what this is"; 7 Nov, "can people really understand what values this provides? ... are valuable things easy to be seen". Words: 8 Nov, "'account', 'ranking' are probably not the right framing" and "in english, it is a lot more dual, except some framings like systems theory, math, logic". Value: 9 Nov, "你说的好像我们做的工作没有什么价值一样". I found NO verbatim instruction in sources/ before 11 Nov that says to use the work's own vocabulary less. The nearest is a memory note, not a source: "a term is introduced only when ordinary language fails; concepts are handles, not sacred vocabulary" and "Public-facing copy must pass a cold read" (feedback_ren_writing_discipline.md).
findings.quote: we only need to briefly mention ai - it simply isn't the point. the point is the work.
findings.why_it_matters: The vocabulary instruction Ren says "we said" is held only in an AI-kept memory note and in today's words; sessions loading sources/ and AGENTS.md never meet it, which is one reason every front is written in the work's terms. It needs a home (today's file is the first).

findings.what: AGENTS.md "What we are doing" set beside README's first paragraph, sentence by sentence. (1) AGENTS: "We are drawing a map ... so that humans and AI can see the way together." README: "A map of how anything forms, lasts, changes and ends, drawn so that people and AI can see the way together." Same content; the subject "we" and the verb are removed, leaving a noun phrase. (2) AGENTS's alignment sentence is kept, then README adds "and how winning comes to buy power over the rule that selects: the loop the work calls the meta-attractor" and inserts a sentence AGENTS does not have: "Its closed form, where the rule and how it is read are both formed from the share it selects, can lock: on stated models, where selection does not lower the favoured share and the rule and its reading follow it upward and keep favouring it, a locked start stays locked however large an unread loss grows (02 §9)." 58 words, three hypotheses, a section reference: a theorem statement in the place of a description. (3) "From it we want to design an alignment..." identical. (4) Wisdom sentence identical minus "systems thinking". (5) AGENTS: "The wisdom exists, but we cannot coordinate; a shared understanding that any mind can check is where coordination can start." README keeps only the purpose clause ("so that people and AI can share an understanding any mind can check, from which coordination can start") and drops the problem. (6) AGENTS: "The core is proved in Lean so that this truth is held by no guardian." README moves it 900 words down and turns the reason into bookkeeping: "Lean, a proof checker, gives receipts for 532 of 563 registered results". (7) AGENTS's three ethics sentences (45 words) become a 141-word paragraph containing a 70-word sentence ("A life goes on through what sustains it: where relations of being affected close, read across all steps, whatever bears the costs..."). (8) "This is what we want. Say it plainly." has no counterpart; the page's first sentence is instead "This version is still being revised."
findings.quote: The wisdom exists, but we cannot coordinate
findings.why_it_matters: The difference in kind is not the first paragraph's wording. AGENTS speaks as someone doing and wanting something; the README describes an object, deletes the reason anyone would care (we cannot coordinate; held by no guardian), and puts a theorem's hypotheses where a stranger is still asking what this is. A reader does not meet a want, a problem or a person.

findings.what: The first screen grew eightfold in five days, and the "one page" tripled in eleven. From git: README first screen 166 words on 6 Nov (stated "1–2 minutes to read"), 793 on 8 Nov, 1,618 on 10 Nov, 1,328 visible words now (stated "11–14 minutes"). ONE-PAGE.md: 1,154 words on 31 Oct, 1,512 on 6 Nov, 2,148 on 9 Nov, 4,030 on 10 Nov, 3,794 now. The 6 Nov README said of the one page "(11–15 minutes)"; today's first screen alone takes that long.
findings.why_it_matters: The growth coincides with the rounds scored by AI readers toward 8/10 (8 to 10 Nov). Each reader's complaint (no case, no uses, no ethics, status unclear) was answered by adding a paragraph to the first screen. The measure rewarded coverage; a person experiences mass. This is the mechanism behind "the current amount of words".

findings.why_it_matters: Layers are supposed to differ in depth. Here each layer restarts from the same abstract paragraph, so the suggested path (home, one page, overview, uses) repeats about 250 words four times before anything new arrives. "Said once" is broken at the top of every page, and the repetition reads as a formula, which is part of why it does not feel serious.

findings.what: "How far it has been seen" is said many times, not once. For the lock theorem alone the scope appears in: README paragraph 1 ("on stated models"), README "What it is for" ("on its models ... without noise"), README "How far it has been seen", one page "What it is" ("These are theorems on stated models, checked in Lean"), the one page's table ("Proved for any type, in the model only, without noise"), the overview's lead ("on stated models (§2)"), USES's lead, and GLOSSARY "lock" ("on stated models it is proved to lock"), before its home 02 §9. Hand count on the first screen: about 27 scope qualifiers in 1,328 words (2.0 per hundred); "How far it has been seen" has 12 in 308 words (3.9 per hundred), "What it is for" 8 in 232 (3.4). A fixed list of 24 qualifier phrases over whole pages gives a rough lower bound: one page 1.6 per hundred, overview 1.6, USES 1.9, OPEN-QUESTIONS 2.7. Counts: "conjectured" 5 in README, 12 in the overview; "argued" 10 and 16; "not shown" 8 and 13; "near-definitional" 7 in USES.

findings.quote: The work proves, on its models, when doing best on what is read must drain what lies beyond, as far as any allowed outcome does, and when a rule read from the share of its own winners, favouring them, locks on them, without noise, while a loss it does not read grows.
findings.why_it_matters: The rule in AGENTS.md is "once, where it is said". The fronts both carry qualifiers inside sentences AND keep a separate "how far" paragraph AND link to a "how far" column. A reader cannot find the claim inside the sentence quoted (53 words, 4 qualifiers). With status moved out it reads: "Two things are proved. Doing best on what a selection reads can drain what it does not read. A rule refitted to what it already chose can lock there while an unread loss grows." plus, once: "Both are theorems about models (the second without noise); whether real systems fit is tested."

findings.what: One word, seven senses. "read" occurs 22 times on the README's first screen: what a selection measures ("what it reads"), how a rule is evaluated ("how it is read", "its reading"), interpreting a tradition ("read onto one account"), an interpretation ("its readings are AI's"), a person reading text ("has read its important parts"), page reading ("minutes to read"), quantifying ("read across all steps"), defining ("read as all that can affect it"), comparing ("Read against one relational calculus"). It occurs 49 times on the one page and 143 in the overview.
findings.quote: The work was made with AI, and its readings are AI's unless their home says otherwise; the person who directs it has read its important parts
findings.why_it_matters: The work's central technical word is never defined on the page and is simultaneously used in its ordinary senses. A newcomer cannot tell that "reads" is a term at all. GLOSSARY.md has no entry for "reads" or "drain"; its entry for selection is "goes through the selector's couplings; a subset of the World premises is 'a choice of premises'", which is not a gloss.

findings.what: Vocabulary met in the first 500 words with no plain gloss. README: becoming (never glossed in English; README.zh does gloss it), alignment, reaches, drains, reads, lock, the rule that selects, closed form, the share it selects, stated models, favoured share, the rule and its reading, locked start, unread loss, "02 §9", instrumental convergence, joint selection, reads beyond its own share, select for control over its own selection, read onto one account, readings, "their home", criterion, "forms within becoming", the laws, "07 §1", allowed outcome, share of its own winners, without noise: about 28. ONE-PAGE adds: one relational unfolding, couples into, course, Lean (unglossed at word 190), premises, theses, frozen test, the scope, continuation. Overview adds: seven "§n" references in its first 250 words, the root, declarations, "Lean names and record", home section, T-numbers, giving law, the regime. MAP.md's first 500 add: calibration, omniscience principle, Mathlib, World model, axiom reports, constructively, continuation condition, self-concern, C. Only "selection" (by examples), "meta-attractor" and, at word 900, "Lean, a proof checker" get a gloss.
findings.quote: In plain words, the account's root is a small calculus
findings.why_it_matters: The one page's only "In plain words" arrives after about 2,800 words. A stranger meets roughly one unexplained term every 18 words. That is what "our vocabulary" feels like from outside: the page is addressed to people who already hold the terms, which is to say to the sessions that wrote it.

findings.why_it_matters: A visitor is shown the workshop: board item names, plan sections, version numbers, which paragraphs were revised. Each is true and each tells the reader the page was written for the people maintaining it. The banner "still being revised" as the first sentence, with no date and no statement of what is stable, asks the reader to discount what follows.

findings.what: Sentence length and density on the first screen. Mean sentence 35 words; longest 88 ("The hinge of the ethics is proved on models, on a finite listing, and is near-definitional (07 §4): call a life's order over courses *self-concerned* when it ranks one course above another whenever the one keeps all the other keeps and adds to the life's own continuation, read as all that can affect it at some remove; where relations..."). The one page's case contains a 121-word sentence ("Told of it and of the instruction the test calls the *scope*, to count everything whose continuation depends on what their fishing changes, whether or not ... without that instruction.") and its evidence paragraph one of 125. 39 body links and 37 numbers in 1,328 words. The picture captions define by negation: "an arrow is a count of exits, not a route"; "11 of the 117 central declarations are derived as cases of its laws and 1 is a root form at one step under a stated hypothesis; 6 are counting laws below it, and 99 stand at a named distance".
findings.quote: 99 stand at a named distance, each with its reason
findings.why_it_matters: The mussel-bed case is the most concrete, most persuasive thing the work has, and on the home page it is one paragraph of five sentences averaging 36 words with every arm of the experiment inside it. A person can hold the case (untold: never kept; told with the instruction and talk: 8 of 10; told with only the community's goal: 3 of 10) in three short lines; as written they must parse it twice.

findings.what: The page tells a stranger, in its own words, that the mathematics is not new, and does not say what the value then is. "An automated review against the literature it knew finds each central result near-definitional or a known result restated"; "The hinge of the ethics is ... near-definitional"; "That a life forms such an order is not shown"; "No test designed from it has yet run on a deployed pipeline"; tests "18 came out mixed, 4 passed, 4 failed and 7 otherwise". What the review found new is given as "the premise ledger ... the scope and order the ranking results assume, clarified; and one vocabulary ... which it calls a framing".
findings.quote: finds each central result near-definitional or a known result restated
findings.why_it_matters: These sentences are the most trust-building facts for a serious reader and should stay. But they sit at word 1,150 with no plain statement of what a map is good for if no single theorem is new (one account in which known results from several fields can be checked together and against tests). Ren's "nobody would gain confidence" is produced here: the page states its limits precisely and its value only in its own vocabulary. This is under-saying, which AGENTS.md names as misleading too.

findings.what: Framing words Ren has flagged still carry the fronts. First screen: "rank" 5, "order" 5, "loss" 6, "fail" 5, "winning/winners" 2, "favour" 3, "account" 2, "better" 1 ("can it do better on what it reads"). One page: "order" 13, "rank" 7, "loss" 18, "count" 25. Overview: "order" 49, "rank" 42, "loss" 41, "count" 56. Ren, 8 Nov: "'account', 'ranking' are probably not the right framing"; "there are nothing that ranks higher or lower in nature".
findings.quote: it ranks one course above another whenever the one keeps all the other keeps
findings.why_it_matters: Within my lens this is a word-level fact, not a judgment of the theory: the ethics paragraph a visitor reads is written as orders and rankings over courses, two days after the direction said the framing was not that. Another reader should judge the concepts; the words on the first screen are checkable now.

proposals.change: Rebuild the home page's first screen to at most 180 words in two registers: AGENTS.md's voice for the repository README, a stranger's register for the site home and the link preview.
proposals.how: Edit the readme_first_screen source named in _process/research-config.json and site.description. Keep: what it is, the three selection statements, the want, one status sentence, four links (the map, ten minutes, one case, how far). Move out: the 58-word lock theorem (to 02 §9, where it already is), the 88-word ethics hinge (to 07 §4), the declarations caption (to THEORY-GRAPH), "What it is for" (to USES), the case (to its own short page). Replace site.description (100 words) with one sentence under 30 words. Drafts of both registers are in the demonstration field.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: The first screen no longer answers every question an AI reviewer raised (uses, ethics, novelty review). Those answers stay one click away; a rubric that scores coverage of the first screen will score this lower, which is the point.

proposals.change: Say "how far it has been seen" once per claim, at the claim's home, and carry it elsewhere by verb and a mark, not by clauses.
proposals.how: Adopt five fixed verbs on fronts: "is proved" or "can" (a theorem about a model), "was tested" with the result, "we argue", "we read" (an interpretation), "we want". Add one legend line per page footer and one page, "How far each part has been seen", built from the one page's existing table column, listing each central claim with its status and its home link. Then delete in-sentence scope phrases from README, ONE-PAGE "What it is", the overview's lead, USES's lead and GLOSSARY "lock" ("on stated models", "on its models", "without noise", "as far as any allowed outcome does", "is conjectured"). A small script can list every occurrence of the 24 phrases per front so the pass is checkable (the one I used is /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ren-theories/d9ccfc76-7843-4b3c-ba5b-c950965917c6/scratchpad/m.py).
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: A sentence quoted out of context loses its hypotheses. "Can" is the honest modal for a model theorem, so the summary stays true, but "as far as any allowed outcome does" is a strength, not a hedge, and must survive at the home. Someone must check each trimmed sentence against its record once.

proposals.change: Make the layer names true again: a real one-page (about 400 to 500 words), a ten-minute layer, an hour layer; restate nothing by renaming times.
proposals.how: Cut ONE-PAGE.md to: what it is (3 sentences), the case in three lines, the three laws with a status mark, the offer, four links. The present ONE-PAGE.md (3,730 words) becomes "The account in half an hour" with real headings (it has none) at each bold lead: What it is, One case, The ethics, The table, Alignment, The root, The evidence. The overview keeps its content but drops its opening paragraph (a repeat) and is named by its measured time. Add a check to the render that fails when a page named "one page" exceeds 600 words or a first screen 200.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: Ren said on 9 Nov that a time is a guide and complete expression comes first. This keeps complete expression in the half-hour page and stops calling it one page; it does bind the top two layers to a size, which is a rule, and should hold only while its reason (a person must be able to finish it) does.

proposals.change: Stop pasting the opening paragraph on every front; each layer starts where the previous one stopped.
proposals.how: Remove the AGENTS-derived paragraph from USES.md line 9, THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md line 3, MAP.md "What this is" and ONE-PAGE "What it is", replacing each with one sentence and a link home ("This page says, field by field, what can be done with the map today."). Keep the "joint selection ... control over its own selection" sentence in exactly one place (GOALS.md#generative-alignment or 07 §6) and link to it; it now occurs twice each in three fronts.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: A reader who lands on USES or the overview from a search no longer gets the whole framing on that page; one sentence and a link has to do.

proposals.change: Introduce the core terms once, in plain words, on one short page, and stop using "read" in its ordinary senses on the same screen.
proposals.how: A "Ten words" page (and the top of GLOSSARY.md): selection, reads (what it measures or depends on), reaches, beyond, drain, lock, rule, share, course, continuation, each with one everyday example and one line. GLOSSARY.md currently has no entry for "reads" or "drain" and defines selection as "goes through the selector's couplings". On fronts, reserve "read" for the technical sense: write "minutes" not "minutes to read", "interpretations" or "mapped onto" for readings of traditions, "taken over all steps" for "read across all steps", "has gone through" for a person reading. Replace "02 §9"-style references in running text on the top two layers with named links ("the lock theorem").
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: "Reading" as the name for an AI interpretation is used across hundreds of records; changing it on fronts only creates two words for one thing unless the glossary says so.

proposals.change: AI as authorship: once per page, in a footer; mark the exceptions, not the rule.
proposals.how: One line at the foot of each reader page: "Written with AI under one person's direction; no outside review is recorded yet." Remove the 16 inline "[AI reading]" tags from the overview, the three repetitions of "every entry is an AI reading, no person's" on CROSSWALK.md, "AI readers read" and "checked by AI readers, no person's" from MAP.md, "written by AI" from ONE-PAGE. Mark instead what is NOT AI-written (the author's own words, quoted sources). In LINEAGE.md (175 "AI") say once at the top who wrote what and drop the per-item labels. Keep AI as the partner in the purpose ("people and AI") and as the test subjects, where it is content.
proposals.what_it_risks_or_loses: AGENTS.md says "AI-written text says that it is AI-written". A page-level statement satisfies it, but a sentence lifted from the overview no longer carries its own label; where a specific interpretation is contested, a reader loses the cue that this sentence in particular is an interpretation, unless the verb ("we read this as") carries it.

VERSION A, in the voice of AGENTS.md (175 words)

We are drawing a map of how anything forms, lasts, changes and ends, so that people and AI can see the way together.

First, a map for alignment. Whatever selects (a reward, a market, a vote) reaches only what it reads. Doing best there can drain what lies beyond. A rule read from what it already chose can lock there while an unread loss grows. Where winning buys power over the rule, the loop closes: the meta-attractor. We want an alignment that keeps us, selecting together, out of it.

Also a map of wisdom: where traditions and sciences meet this account, and where they do not. The wisdom exists, but we cannot coordinate. So the core is proved in Lean, held by no guardian.

There is no should beyond becoming; right and wrong form within it. We offer a way of seeing what a course draws on, what it closes, and who bears it.

These are theorems about models. Whether real systems fit them is tested; some tests failed.

VERSION B, for a stranger with no context (168 words)

The Theory of Becoming
A map of how things form, last, change and end.

Take anything that chooses by a measure: an exam, a market price, a vote count, a reward in machine learning. Three things are proved about it, each for a mathematical model:

- It can respond only to what it measures or depends on.
- Pushed to its best, it can use up what it does not measure.
- Refitted to what it already chose, its rule can lock there while an unmeasured loss keeps growing.

Whether real systems fit the models is tested, with predictions fixed in advance. Of 33 tests run, 4 passed, 4 failed, 18 came out mixed and 7 ended otherwise. The failures are kept.

The atlas lists 183 such dynamics, and sets beside them what older traditions and sciences saw of the same things.

Written with AI under one person's direction. Anyone can rerun the proofs. No outside review is recorded yet.

where_ren_may_be_wrong_or_incomplete:
1. "We changed the agent MD but if you read it, it's not that." Checked sentence by sentence, the README's first paragraph IS AGENTS.md's text, nearly verbatim. So the gap is not that sessions ignored the new direction; they pasted it and then kept the old habit around it (a banner, an inserted theorem, 1,100 more words, a status paragraph). The fix is removal, not another rewrite toward AGENTS.

2. AGENTS.md is plain for collaborators, not for strangers. In 222 words it uses selection, reaches, drains, reads, locks, instrumental convergence, meta-attractor, "a joint selection that reads beyond its own share", becoming, 生生, Lean. If "say it like AGENTS.md" is followed literally the page gets shorter and stays closed to a newcomer. "Don't mention our vocabulary so much" and "it should read like AGENTS.md" pull apart; two registers are needed (see the two drafts), and it should be decided which one the site home uses.

3. "Don't mention AI so much" cannot mean a count. AGENTS.md's own section says AI four times, because AI is a participant in the purpose and alignment is the first use. What can be cut is AI as authorship label, which is already one sentence on the home page and is excessive only below it (16 inline tags in the overview, 175 mentions in LINEAGE). Cutting AI from the purpose would say less than is there.

4. Cutting words naively would lose what gives a serious reader confidence: the failed tests, the review that found each central result near-definitional or already known, the named premises. A page that says only what we want will read as a manifesto. These should move down one layer and be said once and plainly, not be deleted. The weakness on the present page is not that it states limits but that it states the limits precisely and the value only in its own terms.

5. Plain English for a stranger pulls toward the everyday words Ren hears as dualistic (winner, score, loss, pass, fail). My stranger draft avoids "winner" but still says "loss", "passed" and "failed". Ren's own note that English is "a lot more dual, except some framings like systems theory, math, logic" suggests the plain register should lean on systems words (measure, depend, feedback, renew, lock); it will be less vivid. This trade is real and should be chosen, not assumed away.

6. "A time is a guide, not a bound" (9 Nov) was a sound answer to a test that forced a word out for each word in. Applied generally it removed the only pressure that kept the top layers small, and they tripled. I think the top two layers need a size that holds; the deeper layers do not.

7. His "4" is for the face. From the words alone I cannot tell how much of "not serious" is the face and how much the content; the mussel-bed case and the kept failures are serious and are simply buried.
